tour.overview:
Wadi Mujib, the biblical Arnon, cuts a deep canyon down to the Dead Sea, and its reserve, mostly below sea level, is the lowest nature reserve in the world. Its Siq Trail follows the river up a narrow gorge of red sandstone, where you wade, swim and scramble over boulders to a thundering waterfall.

This private day combines the trail with an afternoon at the Dead Sea, with a licensed guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Amman or at the Dead Sea
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; reserve guide for the trail
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate to challenging; you will get completely wet

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Siq Trail of Wadi Mujib.
• The waterfall.
• The Dead Sea.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide handles the reserve permits and the logistics, and the Dead Sea is the perfect place to relax afterwards.

WHO IT SUITS
Active travellers, older children and teenagers who can swim.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a gentle day, choose our Madaba, Mount Nebo and Dead Sea tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Siq Trail is open from about April to October, depending on water levels and flash-flood risk. Life jackets are provided. A minimum age of about 12 applies.

days.name: The Siq Trail of Wadi Mujib and the Dead Sea
days.description:
What to expect: a river canyon adventure and relaxation at the Dead Sea, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrance and a resort day pass with lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:00 and drive down to the Mujib visitor centre on the shore of the Dead Sea. Wearing a life jacket, you enter the canyon over a metal walkway and then walk up the river itself, sometimes ankle-deep, sometimes waist-deep, between smooth walls of red and orange sandstone that close in until only a strip of sky remains. Ropes and ladders help you climb small waterfalls, until you reach the great waterfall at the end of the trail, crashing into a pool. The walk back down is easier, floating with the current in places.

After lunch at a Dead Sea resort, you float in the salty sea, try the black mud and relax by the pools before driving back.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up.
09:15 – Wadi Mujib Siq Trail.
12:30 – Lunch at a Dead Sea resort.
13:30 – Float in the Dead Sea.
16:30 – Drive back.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Wear water shoes or sports sandals with straps and quick-dry clothes.
• Leave phones in a waterproof bag or in the vehicle.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, trail entrance and life jacket, resort day pass with lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: spa treatments, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: When is the Siq Trail open?
faq.answer: Usually from April to October; it closes when flash floods are possible.

faq.question: Do we need to swim?
faq.answer: You should be comfortable in water; life jackets are compulsory and provided.

faq.question: Is there a minimum age?
faq.answer: Yes, about 12 years, set by the reserve.

faq.question: Will we get wet?
faq.answer: Completely. Bring quick-dry clothes and a change for afterwards.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: No; the trail involves climbing and wading.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at a Dead Sea resort.

faq.question: Is it dangerous?
faq.answer: With a guide and in season it is safe; it is never done when floods threaten.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Swimwear, quick-dry clothes and strapped water shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
